newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow telephone sees $150 mln Eurobond in H2.
newsitem.headline: Moscow telephone sees $150 mln Eurobond in H2.

text.p: Russian telecom Moscow City Telephone (MGTS) plans to issue a $150 million Eurobond in the second half of the year and receive a credit rating in September, the company's chief executive said on Wednesday.

"We expect to launch the Eurobond in the second half of this year," Vladimir Lagutin told a news conference. "Now there are a number of working problems with receiving the rating," he said, but added that he expected a September rating for the bond, which would be $150 million as previously expected.
Lagutin said Eurobond plans were also being delayed by an asset revaluation, which MGTS is carrying out in association with American Appraisals.
MGTS had said earlier that CSFB and Salomon Brothers would lead the Eurobond.
MGTS is one of the highest profile Russian telecoms. Ordinary shares traded at $1,600 on the Russian Trading System at 0840 GMT after $1,500 at the close on Tuesday.
